acs/acs1.uncertainty_metrics: 1-year ACS estimates, published only for geographies with 65,000+ residents. Sampling noise dominates and runs materially larger than acs/acs5 (fewer sampled households per estimate); CV follows the same 1/sqrt(N) law. [Source: findings report Section 2 vocabulary + general methodology - needs mentor review]

acs/acs1/pums.uncertainty_metrics: 1-year Public-Use Microdata. No per-estimate MOE; ships with 80 replicate weights, analyst computes SEs. Smaller sample than acs/acs5/pums. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

acs/acs1/subject.uncertainty_metrics: Same 1-year sampling regime as acs/acs1 with subject-table cell definitions. Smaller sample vs. acs/acs5/subject means wider MOEs and higher CVs at every geography level. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

acs/acs5.composite_role_note: primary CV source for every ACS geography

acs/acs5.uncertainty_metrics: 90% margin of error ships with every published estimate; CVs run ~1% at county, ~13% at tract, ~20% at block group for median income - and can exceed 1.0 for small subgroup counts (Findings 1-2). Allocation rates carry no MOE of their own and are statistically independent of the MOE (Findings 8-9). [Source: findings report Sections 3 + 5]

acs/acs5/cprofile.uncertainty_metrics: Comparison profile tables (year-over-year change) derived from ACS 5-year. Change estimates carry their own MOEs computed from both endpoint MOEs; two overlapping 5-year windows share ~4 of 5 sample years, so change MOEs are wider than either endpoint. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

acs/acs5/profile.uncertainty_metrics: Pre-computed profile tables derived from acs/acs5 detailed tables. Inherits ACS 5-year sampling noise: MOEs ship on every cell, CV scales as 1/sqrt(N behind the estimate). [general methodology - needs mentor review]

acs/acs5/subject.uncertainty_metrics: Same sampling-noise regime as acs/acs5. Subject tables include poverty (B17001) - typical tract CV ~0.38 - and small-subgroup cells (e.g., Black 65+ at ~0.89), which the findings report shows can be tamed via aggregation using the Bureau MOE-combination formula. [Source: findings report Section 3, Finding 2]

cbp.uncertainty_metrics: County Business Patterns - administrative-record establishment counts + payroll + employment. Suppressed cells are flagged; the file uses "noise infusion" (multiplicative perturbation) on employment to protect small-cell confidentiality. Noise flags on each cell indicate low/moderate/high perturbation. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

cre.uncertainty_metrics: Community Resilience Estimates - modeled tract-level social-vulnerability indicators built from ACS microdata via small-area estimation. Publishes MOEs computed from replicate-weight variance of the underlying microdata. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

dec/dhc.uncertainty_metrics: Full-count 2020 Decennial data protected by the Disclosure Avoidance System (differential privacy). Noise is a near-fixed absolute cost per place - small relative impact at county level, but overwhelming at block level (Finding 4). Geography TYPE matters: block groups carry ~9x tract noise for the same population (Finding 5). [Source: findings report Section 4]

geo/tiger.uncertainty_metrics: TIGER / Line + cartographic boundary geometry. No statistical uncertainty in a sampling / DP-noise sense; positional accuracy is documented per file (roughly meter-scale for cartographic boundaries, coarser for generalized files). Vintage-to-vintage geometry changes (annexations, redistricting) are the main gotcha. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

pdb/blockgroup.uncertainty_metrics: Planning Database - pre-computed operational metrics (mail-return rates, hard-to-count indicators) built from ACS 5-year + prior Decennial. Uncertainty inherits from the source estimates; the PDB itself does not publish new MOEs. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

pep/housing.uncertainty_metrics: Housing Unit Estimates - modeled annual housing-unit counts using building-permit inputs plus estimates of losses. No published MOE; revised annually with the rest of PEP. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

pep/population.uncertainty_metrics: Population Estimates Program - modeled annual population counts built forward from the last Decennial using vital records, migration, and administrative data. No published MOE; "uncertainty" is revealed via the annual Vintage revisions (each new vintage restates prior years). [general methodology - needs mentor review]

popproj/pop.uncertainty_metrics: Population Projections - model-based projections of the U.S. population by age/sex/race/origin decades forward. No MOE; the Bureau publishes alternative scenarios (main / high-immigration / low-immigration / zero-immigration) to bracket assumption uncertainty. [general methodology - needs mentor review]

sipp.uncertainty_metrics: Survey of Income and Program Participation - longitudinal household panel. No per-estimate MOE published in most tables; replicate weights ship with the microdata for user-computed SEs. [general methodology - needs mentor review]
